notes: Sol 313 (5-6 Jan 2022, Ls ~153) is the day the January 2022 regional dust storm reached Jezero (late morning, per Lemmon et al.). All values were computed from the PDS CSVs, not copied from a paper. Values at the snapshot time are 30-minute means over LMST 11:45-12:15 (LTST ~12:34, ~07:15 UTC on 2022-01-06). air_temp_c = mean of the three mast ATS sensors (ATS_LOCAL_TEMP1-3, ~1.45 m); min_sol/max_sol are the extreme 1-s values that sol (04:58 and 13:38 LMST). pressure_pa = sol mean (mean of the 24 hourly means); 613.3 Pa at the snapshot time; the sol range was 583.5-642.9 Pa, and this afternoon had the storm's deepest pressure minimum. relative_humidity_pct = 0.0 at midday (MEDA RHS hourly means are 0.00 from 09 to 17 LMST); the sol peak was 34.6 % at 04:28 LMST. wind_ms = mean horizontal speed; peak gusts were 22.5 m/s at 09:48 LMST and 22.2 m/s at 13:08 LMST (13:42 LTST, matching the 22 m/s peak reported by Lemmon et al.). WIND IS ONLY PARTIAL: derived wind data on sol 313 stops at ~13:08 LMST (the boom-2 sensor was damaged by wind-blown debris that afternoon), and the derived WS files for sols 314-315 contain only fill values (999999999). dust_opacity is null because no direct measurement exists for sol 313: the Mastcam-Z optical-depth record has no points between sol 311 (tau 0.327 at 544 nm, pre-storm) and sol 319 (0.458). The storm peak was ~2 (Lemmon et al. 2022). See dust_opacity_context. Sensors with data on sol 313: ATS, PS, RHS, TIRS, WS (until ~13:08 LMST). Not used: RDS (would need a radiative-transfer retrieval to give tau).

sources: Lemmon, M. T. (2026). The Perseverance Rover's Mastcam-Z Visible Aerosol Optical Depth Record, Mendeley Data v2, doi:10.17632/gktjp9jptb.2 (file m20-ztau-merged-1717.txt, marked PRELIMINARY by the author) — https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/gktjp9jptb/2
